key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥ 20%) include hyperphosphatemia, alopecia, diarrhea, nail toxicity, fatigue, dysgeusia, nausea, constipation, stomatitis, dry eye, dry mouth, decreased appetite, vomiting, arthralgia, abdominal pain, hypophosphatemia, back pain, and dry skin. Most important serious risks are ocular toxicity (retinal pigment epithelial detachment [RPED] occurred in 6% of 466 patients, Grade 3-4 in 0.6%) and hyperphosphatemia (reported in 92% of 466 patients).

Among the 466 patients who received pemigatinib across clinical trials, retinal pigment epithelial detachment (RPED), which can cause symptoms such as blurred vision, visual floaters, or photopsia, occurred in 6% of patients, including Grade 3-4 events in 0.6% of patients.
Among 466 patients who received pemigatinib across clinical trials, hyperphosphatemia was reported in 92% of patients based on laboratory values above the upper limit of normal.
